    Macroeconomics

    Macroeconomics: growth, business cycles, investment, and trade.

    It also holds international trade and mortal monetary economies.

    BrockMirmanGrowthSystem(K=0.2, *, alpha=1 / 3, beta=0.95, z_low=0.9, z_high=1.1, persistence=0.9, regime=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The Brock-Mirman economy.

    It is the optimal growth of a representative agent whose productivity is Markov. A representative consumer maximises E_0 sum_t beta^t ln C_t subject to K_{t+1} = Y_t - C_t, with full depreciation and the output Y_t = z_t K_t^alpha of a representative firm, whose productivity z_t follows a Markov chain. The solution is the linear consumption rule C_t = (1 - alpha beta) Y_t, C = 0.68 Y for alpha = 1/3 and beta = 0.95, so the capital follows K_{t+1} = alpha beta z_t K_t^alpha and ln K is a stationary autoregression around (ln(alpha beta) + E ln z) / (1 - alpha). This is the standard model that Caiani et al. (2016, Section 1.1.4, Eqs. 1.3 to 1.9) compare with an agent-based economy. The source leaves the chain open, so the productivity takes two levels that stay with the probability persistence.

    The system has the capital economy.K and the regime economy.regime. The observables of the system are economy.productivity, economy.output, and economy.consumption.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    K float

    The initial capital.

    		 0.2
    alpha float

    The capital share of the technology.

    		 1 / 3
    beta float

    The discount factor of the household.

    		 0.95
    z_low float

    The low productivity.

    		 0.9
    z_high float

    The high productivity.

    		 1.1
    persistence float

    The probability that the productivity keeps its level from one period to the next.

    		 0.9
    regime int

    The initial regime, 0 for the low and 1 for the high productivity.

    		 0
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.macroeconomics import BrockMirmanGrowthSystem
>>> BrockMirmanGrowthSystem(beta=0.9).prepare().system_.elements[0].beta
0.9

    BusinessElement(label, visual=None, *, money=0.0, loans=0.0, stock=0.0, wage=4.0, price=1.0, owner=-1.0, workers=1.0, vacancies=1.0, revenue=0.0, interest=0.003, repayment=0.004, adjustment=0.05, stock_limit=30.0)

    Bases: Element

    Firm on a patch that harvests with its workers and sells food in its shop.

    It pays wages with money it borrows. Every step the workers pool their labour on the firm's patch, the firm pays each the wage, borrowing what it lacks from the bank, and pays the interest and a share of the principal of its loans. A firm that sold out raises its price, and one with a stock above stock_limit lowers it and lays a worker off. Otherwise a firm posts vacancies up to the workforce that harvests the whole capacity of its patch, raises the wage while a vacancy went unfilled, and lowers it while its sales fall short of its wage bill. Profits above twice the wage bill go to the owner, and a firm without a living owner passes to one of its workers.

    def produce(self, agent: BusinessView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Harvest with the workers, pay wages and the bank, and adjust.

    It then pays a dividend to the owner.

    Args:
        agent:
            The firm.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    people = BusinessElement._get_people_by_id(system)
    workers = [person for person in people.values() if person.employer == agent.id]
    bank = system.get_agents('bank', CentralBankView)[0]
    patch = SettlerElement._get_patch_here(agent)
    sold_out = agent.stock <= 0
    for worker in workers:
        worker.move_to(agent.location)
    labour = sum(worker.labour for worker in workers)
    harvest = min(patch.food, max(labour - patch.resistance, 0.0))
    patch.food -= harvest
    agent.stock += harvest
    bill = agent.wage * len(workers)
    self._borrow(agent, bank, bill - agent.money)
    for worker in workers:
        transfer(agent, worker, agent.wage, 'money')
        worker.harvested = worker.need
    self._pay_debt(agent, bank)
    self._adjust(agent, workers, patch, sold_out)
    agent.workers, agent.revenue = float(len(workers)), 0.0
    owner = agent.get_referenced('owner')
    if not isinstance(owner, SettlerView) and workers:
        owner = workers[0]
        agent.owner = float(owner.id)
    if isinstance(owner, SettlerView) and agent.money > 2 * bill:
        transfer(agent, owner, agent.money - 2 * bill, 'money')

    CapitalStockSystem(capital=100.0, *, investment_fraction=0.2, output_per_capital=1 / 3, lifetime=15.0, label='system')

    Bases: DynamicalSystem

    Meadows' capital stock, grown by reinvested output and drained by depreciation.

    The stock follows dK/dt = investment_fraction * output_per_capital * K - K / lifetime. It grows exponentially when the capital lives longer than 1 / (investment_fraction * output_per_capital), declines when it lives shorter, and stays in dynamic equilibrium otherwise. The system has the capital stock economy.K.

    The average lifetime of the capital.

    label str

    CategorizedPurchasingPowerSystem(policy=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), policy_time=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0), *, feedback=True, A=A_MATRIX, B=B_MATRIX, C=C_MATRIX, D=D_MATRIX, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Forrest's categorized purchasing power of money.

    Its three sectors can be steered one by one by feedback. The economy is split into the sectors of the basic, the desired, and the luxurious living conditions, with the gaps z_i = D_i - S_i between the demand and the supply of money of each, which the categorized monetary and fiscal policies x_i move through z' = A z + B x, and the indices of the sectors y = C z + D x, from the zero state (Forrest 2018, Eqs. 22.6 and 22.7). The policies of one sector act on all of them. By Theorem 11.3 and Example 11.2 the system can be decoupled by feedback into the systems w' = A w + B_i x_i and y_i = C_i w + D_i x_i of the sectors (Eqs. 22.9 to 22.12), whose market reactions keep each index on its own policy, so money poured into the luxury sector leaves the basic sector alone. The source gives no numbers, so the matrices are illustrative, with a stable A and a stable A - B D^-1 C, and the policies are steps.

    The system has the gaps economy.z1 to economy.z3 and, with feedback, the decoupled states economy.w11 to economy.w33. The observables of the system are the indices economy.y1 to economy.y3 and the inputs of the economy economy.u1 to economy.u3.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    policy Sequence[float]

    The size of the step policy of every sector.

    policy_time Sequence[float]

    The time of the step policy of every sector.

    feedback bool

            ('firms.deposits', 'households.deposits', lambda s: s.firms.wage_share * s.firms.sales, 'wages'),
            ('firms.deposits', 'bank.deposits', lambda s: s.bank.interest * s.firms.loans, 'interest'),
            ('bank.deposits', 'households.deposits', lambda s: s.bank.payout * s.bank.deposits, 'dividends'),
            (
                'firms.deposits',
                'households.deposits',
                lambda s: s.firms.distribution * s.firms.deposits,
                'profits',
            ),
            (
                Source('lending'),
                'firms.deposits',
                lambda s: CircuitInteraction._get_lending(s.firms, s.bank),
                'lending',
            ),
            ('firms.deposits', Sink('repayment'), lambda s: s.firms.repayment * s.firms.loans, 'repayments'),
        ],
    )
    self.households = households
    self.firms = firms
    self.bank = bank

    def harvest(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Harvest every occupied patch and share the food among the people on it.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the interaction.
    """
    cells: dict[tuple[int, ...], list[SettlerView]] = {}
    for person in system.get_agents('people', SettlerView):
        cells.setdefault(SettlerElement._get_cell(person), []).append(person)
    for group in cells.values():
        patch = SettlerElement._get_patch_here(group[0])
        labour = sum(person.labour for person in group if person.age >= person.maturity)
        harvest = min(patch.food, max(labour - patch.resistance, 0.0))
        patch.food -= harvest
        for person in group:
            person.food += harvest / len(group)
            person.harvested = harvest / len(group)

    CreditNetworksSystem(firms=100, banks=10, *, sample=3, intensity=4.0, leverage=1.0, mean_return=0.03, volatility=0.3, net_worth=10.0, equity=100.0, alpha=0.1, capital_ratio=0.1, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    A credit market where firms sample banks and switch to cheaper lenders.

    Defaults hit the lenders. Every step the banks quote rates that fall with their equity, every firm samples sample banks and switches from its lender to the cheapest of them with probability 1 - exp(intensity * (r_new - r_old) / r_new), borrows, and invests at a random return. Interest and write-offs of defaulted firms move net worth between firms and banks, so the total net worth changes only by the firms' returns and the entrants' net worth. A higher intensity of switching concentrates the loans in the cheapest banks and narrows the spread of the rates that firms pay.

    The system has the groups firms and banks, the market credit with its reporter credit.spread, and the observables herfindahl, largest_share, bank_equity, firm_worth, returns, injected, defaults, and bad_debt.

    def count(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Count the births and deaths of the step and remove the dead.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the interaction.
    """
    people = system.get_agents('people', SettlerView)
    living = [person for person in people if person.fate == ALIVE]
    dead = [person for person in people if person.fate != ALIVE]
    system.report('births', float(sum(person.age == 0 for person in living)))
    system.report('starvations', float(sum(person.fate == STARVED for person in dead)))
    system.report('old_age', float(sum(person.fate == AGED for person in dead)))
    for person in dead:
        self._settle(person, living, system)

    ExchangeRatesSystem(exports=32.0, imports=34.0, *, home_price=1.2, inflation=0.1, export_elasticity=-1.0, import_elasticity=-1.0, floating=True, demand=52.0, government=50.0, world_price=1.0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Hamill and Gilbert's staged adjustment of trade and the exchange rate.

    The adjustment follows a rise in home prices. The economy starts in balance at the exchange rate E = M * PW / (X * PH), in units of World currency per unit of Home currency, with the export and import volumes and prices of the United Kingdom in 1999 by default. Home prices rise by inflation at the first stage. At every stage a floating rate takes the value that balances the currency market at the current volumes, a fixed rate stays, and the volumes respond to the prices of the stage before with constant price elasticities. The book follows two stages, the default.

    The system has the economy home, the balance of trade at home prices balance, the real exchange rate real_rate, and the output output.

    Bases: Element

    Firm that borrows in proportion to its net worth and invests.

    It invests at a random return, and defaults on negative worth. Every step the firm asks for leverage times its net worth from its bank, invests its net worth and the loan at the return mean_return + volatility * z, and pays the interest. When its net worth becomes negative it repays what it can, the bank writes off the rest, and a new firm with the net worth entry replaces it.

    @staticmethod
def get_default() -> tuple[tuple[str, Callable[[FirmView, SystemView], float]], ...]:
    """Return the states a firm sets after its return.

    A firm that defaults takes those of an entrant.

    Returns:
        default:
            The name of every state and the function of its value, of the firm and the system view.
    """
    worth = FirmElement.get_worth
    return (
        ('injected', lambda agent, system: agent.entry if worth(agent) < 0 else agent.injected),
        ('defaulted', lambda agent, system: 1.0 if worth(agent) < 0 else agent.defaulted),
        ('partner', lambda agent, system: -1.0 if worth(agent) < 0 else agent.partner),
        ('net_worth', lambda agent, system: agent.entry if worth(agent) < 0 else worth(agent)),
    )

    @staticmethod
def get_plan() -> tuple[tuple[str, Callable[[FirmView, SystemView], float]], ...]:
    """Return the states a firm sets in the plan of a step.

    It requests a loan of `leverage` times its net worth.

    Returns:
        plan:
            The name of every state and the function of its value, of the firm and the system view.
    """
    return (
        ('demand', lambda agent, system: agent.leverage * agent.net_worth),
        ('loan', lambda agent, system: 0.0),
        ('rate', lambda agent, system: 0.0),
        ('defaulted', lambda agent, system: 0.0),
        ('injected', lambda agent, system: 0.0),
    )

    @staticmethod
def get_return(agent: FirmView, system: SystemView) -> float:
    """Return the return on the net worth and the loan invested.

    The rate of return is normal and at least -1.

    Args:
        agent:
            The firm.

        system:
            The system view of the investment.

    Returns:
        gross_return:
            The return of the step.
    """
    draw = agent.mean_return + agent.volatility * system.rng.standard_normal()
    return (agent.net_worth + agent.loan) * max(draw, -1.0)

    @staticmethod
def get_worth(agent: FirmView) -> float:
    """Return the net worth after the return and the interest.

    It is negative for a firm that defaults.

    Args:
        agent:
            The firm.

    Returns:
        worth:
            The net worth before a default.
    """
    return agent.net_worth + agent.gross_return - agent.loan * agent.rate

    FoodMarketInteraction(label, *, requesters, providers, rule=RandomSearchSpec(), reserve='reserve', quantity='quantity', cap='cap', transfers=(), phase=None, on_match=None)

    Bases: MatchingInteraction[SystemView]

    Food market in which people short of food buy from the cheapest shop in sight.

    They buy in random order, from stocked shops. A matching of the people, who request their shortfall of food for reserve steps within the budget of their money, with the firms, which provide their stock at their price. Every purchase moves the money to the firm, which books it as revenue, and the food to the buyer. Build it with PartnerMatchingSpec(sight, 'score', score=FoodMarketInteraction.score, value='provider'), whose score prefers the lowest price. Besides the reporters of a matching, the reporter gdp sums the value of the sales of a step.

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.core.specs import PartnerSpec
>>> from skcomplex.systems.economics.macroeconomics import FoodMarketInteraction
>>> rule = PartnerMatchingSpec(5.0, 'score', score=FoodMarketInteraction.score, value='provider')
>>> FoodMarketInteraction('shops', requesters='people', providers='businesses', rule=rule).reports[-1]
'gdp'

    @staticmethod
def score(person: object, firm: object) -> float:
    """Return the score of a firm for a person, higher for a lower price.

    Args:
        person:
            The person that buys.

        firm:
            The firm that sells.

    Returns:
        score:
            Minus the price of the firm.
    """
    del person
    return -float(firm.price) if isinstance(firm, BusinessView) else -math.inf

    @staticmethod
def sell(match: MatchSpec, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Book the value of a sale as revenue of the firm.

    Args:
        match:
            The match of a buyer with a firm.

        system:
            The system view of the market.
    """
    del system
    if isinstance(match.provider, BusinessView):
        match.provider.revenue += match.quantity * match.value

    FractionalReserveBankingSystem(customers=100, banks=5, *, base_money=1000.0, ratio=0.1, new_ratio=None, change_at=150.0, spending=0.1, repayment=0.05, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Customers and banks whose lending of excess reserves multiplies the base money.

    The multiplier is 1 / ratio. The base money starts as equal deposits of the customers, held as reserves by their banks, picked at random. Every step the customers pay a share of their deposits to random customers and repay a share of their loans from their deposits, and every bank lends its reserves above the required share of its deposits. The loans are spent and redeposited at random banks. The reserves stay equal to the base money, so the broad money, the sum of deposits, settles near base_money / ratio. A regulator changes the reserve ratio to new_ratio at change_at, and the broad money moves to the new multiplier.

    The system has the groups customers and banks, the institution regulator, and the observables broad_money, reserves, and loans.

    InvestingFirmElement(label, visual=None, *, A=1.0, K=1.0, Z=0.0, B=0.0, Y=0.0, P=0.0, gamma=1.1, phi=0.1, r=0.1, pbar=0.01)

    Bases: Element

    Firm of the toy business-cycle system.

    It invests a share of its last profit and sells at a random price. Every period the firm invests I = gamma * Z, accumulates capital K = K + I, produces Y = phi * K, borrows B = max(K - A, 0), sells at the price P = pbar + 2 U(0, 1), earns Z = P * Y - r * K, and adds the profit to its net worth A. A firm whose net worth turns negative is replaced by an entrant with A = K = 1 and Z = 0.

    @staticmethod
def get_steps() -> tuple[tuple[str, str, Callable[[InvestingFirmView, SystemView], float]], ...]:
    """Return the steps of a period in their order.

    Each is a label, a state, and the function of its next value. A firm invests, produces, borrows, sells, earns,
    adds the profit to its net worth, and, when the net worth turns negative, is replaced by an entrant, whose
    profit, capital, and net worth the last three steps reset.

    Returns:
        steps:
            The label of every step, the state it sets, and the function of its next value of the firm and the
            system view.
    """
    return (
        ('investment', 'K', lambda agent, system: agent.K + agent.gamma * agent.Z),
        ('production', 'Y', lambda agent, system: agent.phi * agent.K),
        ('borrowing', 'B', lambda agent, system: max(agent.K - agent.A, 0.0)),
        ('pricing', 'P', InvestingFirmElement.get_price),
        ('profit', 'Z', lambda agent, system: agent.P * agent.Y - agent.r * agent.K),
        ('accumulation', 'A', lambda agent, system: agent.A + agent.Z),
        ('entry_profit', 'Z', lambda agent, system: 0.0 if agent.A < 0 else agent.Z),
        ('entry_capital', 'K', lambda agent, system: 1.0 if agent.A < 0 else agent.K),
        ('entry_worth', 'A', lambda agent, system: 1.0 if agent.A < 0 else agent.A),
    )

    LabourMarketInteraction(label, *, requesters, providers, rule=RandomSearchSpec(), reserve='reserve', quantity='quantity', cap='cap', transfers=(), phase=None, on_match=None)

    Bases: MatchingInteraction[SystemView]

    Labour market in which unemployed adults take the best-paying vacancy in sight.

    They take it in random order. A matching of the people, who request a job, with the firms, which provide their vacancies: a person whose hireable limit admits a job takes the firm of the highest wage within its sight that still has a vacancy, and moves to it. Build it with PartnerMatchingSpec(sight, 'score', score=LabourMarketInteraction.score, value='provider').

...     reserve=('hireable', 'reserve'),
...     quantity=('quantity', 'vacancies'),
...     on_match=LabourMarketInteraction.hire,
... ).providers

    @staticmethod
def hire(match: MatchSpec, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Employ a matched person at its firm and move it there.

    Args:
        match:
            The match of a person with a firm.

        system:
            The system view of the market.
    """
    del system
    person, firm = match.requester, match.provider
    if isinstance(person, SettlerView) and isinstance(firm, BusinessView):
        person.employer = float(firm.id)
        person.move_to(firm.location)

    @staticmethod
def get_income(agent: LenderView, system: SystemView) -> float:
    """Return the interest a bank earns in the step.

    It is less what its defaulting borrowers cannot repay.

    Args:
        agent:
            The bank.

        system:
            The system view of the settlement.

    Returns:
        income:
            The change of the equity.
    """
    borrowers = LenderElement._get_borrowers(agent, system)
    return sum(firm.loan * firm.rate + min(FirmElement.get_worth(firm), 0.0) for firm in borrowers)

def get_quote() -> tuple[tuple[str, Callable[[LenderView, SystemView], float]], ...]:
    """Return the states a bank sets in the plan of a step.

    Mark0EconomyInteraction(label, *, rule=None, phase=None, firms, c0=0.5, beta=2.0, gamma=0.01, eta_minus=0.2, ratio=2.0, delta=0.02, theta=3.0, phi=0.1, zeta=1.0, omega=0.2, f=0.5, shock_time=100.0, shock_length=0.0, dc=0.0, dzeta=0.0, kappa=1.0, offset=1.25, credit='none')

    Bases: PolicyRuleInteraction[SystemView]

    Representative household and bank of the Mark-0 economy.

    They run the firms through one month every step. Every step the firms adjust their workforce, prices, and wages by the rules of thumb of Mark-0 (Eqs. 11 to 17 of Sharma et al. 2020) from the demand and the profit of the last month, pay their wages, and sell to the household, whose consumption budget c (S + W + rho_d S) (Eq. 5) splits among the firms by the logit demand of their prices relative to the mean price (Eq. 9). Firms pay interest and, when profitable with positive cash, a share delta of their cash as dividends (Eqs. 18 and 19). A firm whose debt to payroll Phi = -E / (W N) reaches the bankruptcy threshold Theta defaults, its debt falls on the bank, which moves the loan and deposit rates (Eqs. 21 and 22), and a bankrupt firm is revived with probability phi per month at the mean price and wage. Following the simplifications of the source, inflation expectations, the feedback of inflation on consumption, the effect of fragility on hiring, and the central bank are switched off, so the base rate is zero.

    During the shock, from shock_time for shock_length months, the productivity falls by the share dzeta and the consumption propensity by the share dc. The credit policy 'naive' lifts the threshold during the shock and restores it at once after it, and 'adaptive' restores it to max(offset <Phi>, Theta) with the production-weighted mean fragility <Phi> (Eq. 24). At the end of the shock the household's savings are multiplied by kappa, the helicopter money.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the economy.

    		 required
    rule None

    phase str | None

    def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Run one month of the economy.

    It adjusts, pays, sells, distributes, defaults, revives, and sets the rates.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the economy.
    """
    firms = sorted(system.get_agents('firms', Mark0FirmView), key=lambda firm: firm.id)
    names = ('workforce', 'demand', 'price', 'wage', 'cash', 'profit', 'active')
    keys = ('n', 'd', 'p', 'w', 'e', 'profit', 'active')
    state = {key: np.array([getattr(firm, name) for firm in firms]) for key, name in zip(keys, names, strict=True)}
    store = system.storage
    month = int(self._get_stored(system, 'month', 0.0))
    savings, inflation_ema = self._get_stored(system, 'savings', 0.0), self._get_stored(
        system,
        'inflation_ema',
        0.0,
    )
    rho_l, rho_d = self._get_stored(system, 'rho_l', 0.0), self._get_stored(system, 'rho_d', 0.0)
    start, length = system.get_parameter('shock_time'), system.get_parameter('shock_length')
    shocked = start <= month < start + length
    zeta = system.get_parameter('zeta') * (1 - system.get_parameter('dzeta') * shocked)
    c = system.get_parameter('c0') * (1 - system.get_parameter('dc') * shocked)
    if length > 0 and month == start + length:
        savings *= system.get_parameter('kappa')
    size = len(firms)
    if month > 0:
        state['sales'] = np.asarray(store['sales'])
        state['interest'] = np.asarray(store['interest'])
        self._adjust(system, state, zeta, 1 - state['n'].sum() / size)
    active = state['active'] > 0
    production = zeta * state['n']
    bill = state['w'] * state['n']
    wages = float(bill.sum())
    state['e'] = state['e'] - bill
    mean_price = self._get_weighted(state['p'][active], production[active])
    mean_wage = self._get_weighted(state['w'][active], production[active])
    budget = c * (savings + wages + rho_d * savings)
    weights = np.where(active, np.exp(-system.get_parameter('beta') * state['p'] / mean_price), 0.0)
    state['d'] = budget * weights / (state['p'] * weights.sum())
    sales = state['p'] * np.minimum(production, state['d'])
    interest = rho_d * np.maximum(state['e'], 0.0) + rho_l * np.minimum(state['e'], 0.0)
    state['e'] = state['e'] + sales + interest
    state['profit'] = sales - bill + interest
    savings += wages + rho_d * savings - float(sales.sum())
    dividends = np.where((state['profit'] > 0) & (state['e'] > 0), system.get_parameter('delta') * state['e'], 0.0)
    state['e'] -= dividends
    savings += float(dividends.sum())
    fragility_of = np.divide(-state['e'], bill, out=np.zeros(size), where=bill > 0)
    fragility = self._get_weighted(fragility_of[active], production[active])
    threshold = self._get_threshold(system, month, fragility)
    defaulted = active & (fragility_of >= threshold)
    losses = float(-state['e'][defaulted].sum())
    for key in ('n', 'd', 'e', 'profit', 'active'):
        state[key] = np.where(defaulted, 0.0, state[key])
    unemployment = 1 - state['n'].sum() / size
    revived = (state['active'] == 0) & ~defaulted & (system.rng.random(size) < system.get_parameter('phi'))
    start_size = unemployment * system.rng.random(size)
    state['n'] = np.where(revived, start_size, state['n'])
    state['p'] = np.where(revived, mean_price, state['p'])
    state['w'] = np.where(revived, mean_wage, state['w'])
    state['active'] = np.where(revived, 1.0, state['active'])
    previous = self._get_stored(system, 'price', mean_price)
    inflation = (mean_price - previous) / previous
    inflation_ema = system.get_parameter('omega') * inflation + (1 - system.get_parameter('omega')) * inflation_ema
    debts, deposits = float(-np.minimum(state['e'], 0.0).sum()), float(np.maximum(state['e'], 0.0).sum())
    f = system.get_parameter('f')
    rho_l = f * losses / debts if debts > 0 else 0.0
    rho_d = -(1 - f) * losses / (savings + deposits) if savings + deposits > 0 else 0.0
    store.update(
        month=month + 1,
        savings=savings,
        inflation_ema=inflation_ema,
        rho_l=rho_l,
        rho_d=rho_d,
        price=mean_price,
        sales=np.where(defaulted, 0.0, sales),
        interest=np.where(defaulted, 0.0, interest),
    )
    for index, firm in enumerate(firms):
        for key, name in zip(keys, names, strict=True):
            setattr(firm, name, float(state[key][index]))
    reported = {
        'unemployment': 1 - state['n'].sum() / size,
        'inflation': inflation,
        'output': float((zeta * state['n']).sum()),
        'savings': savings,
        'fragility': fragility,
        'bankruptcies': float(defaulted.sum()),
        'threshold': min(threshold, 1e9),
        'price': mean_price,
        'wage': mean_wage,
    }
    for name, value in reported.items():
        system.report(name, value)

    Mark0System(n_firms=500, *, c0=0.5, beta=2.0, gamma=0.01, eta_minus=0.2, ratio=2.0, delta=0.02, theta=3.0, phi=0.1, shock_time=100.0, shock_length=0.0, dc=0.0, dzeta=0.0, kappa=1.0, credit='none', random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The Mark-0 economy of Sharma, Bouchaud, and co-authors.

    It has a Covid shock to supply and demand. Firms produce perishable goods with a linear technology, sell them to a representative household at prices they adjust by rules of thumb, hire and fire by the gap between production and demand, and borrow from a representative bank, defaulting when their debt to payroll exceeds the threshold Theta (Sharma et al. 2020, Section 2). A month is a step, the money starts at zero, and the economy is stock-flow consistent apart from the written-off debts and the helicopter money. With the defaults of Table 1 the economy sits in the full employment phase. A lockdown lowers the productivity and the consumption propensity for shock_length months, after which a mild shock recovers in a V shape and a strong one tips the economy into an L-shaped recession of high unemployment, which easy credit and helicopter money can prevent. The source summarizes the model of earlier papers, so the initial firms (a workforce between 0.9 and 1, prices around 1, unit wages, no cash) and revived firms (the mean price and wage and a random share of the unemployed) follow Gualdi et al. (2015), and the demand reads prices relative to the mean price.

    The system has the group firms and the economy economy, whose reporters are economy.unemployment, economy.inflation, economy.output, economy.savings, economy.fragility, economy.bankruptcies, economy.threshold, economy.price, and economy.wage.

    MetaphoriaSystem(n_people=100, *, mode='hunter_gatherer', shape=(20, 20), max_food=15.0, max_resistance=5.0, regrowth=1.0, need=2.0, labour=5.0, interest=0.003, repayment=0.004, n_firms=5, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Gooding's Metaphoria.

    It is a mortal population of hunter-gatherers or of a monetary economy. Patches of a periodic lattice hold food that grows back to a random capacity and resist harvesting with a random resistance. People need food every step, age, die of starvation or old age, and have children who inherit their propensities to breed, explore, found firms, and quit jobs, with mutations, so the propensities evolve under the test of survival. Hunter-gatherers pool the labour of the adults on a patch and share the harvest. In the monetary economy firms harvest with paid workers, sell the food in shops, and borrow the wages from a bank that creates money as loans, so the money of all holders sums to zero at every step. Gooding found the hunter-gatherers stable, and the monetary population smaller and less healthy, with money concentrating to a Gini coefficient near 0.5. On land where the hunter-gatherers thrive the monetary population dwindles towards extinction, and with abundant food it lives on with persistent starvation.

    The system has the group patches, one per cell, the variable group people, the reporters census.births, census.starvations, and census.old_age, and the observables population and money_gini. The monetary economy adds the variable group businesses, the group bank, and the reporter shops.gdp.

    NetworkHerdingSystem(theta=None, x=None, *, gamma=1.0, sigma=0.1, n_agents=50, density=0.1, herding=0.5, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Agents whose linear choices herd on the past choices of linked agents.

    They herd on the agents they are linked to. The choice of agent i is c_it = sum_j theta_ij c_j,t-1 + gamma x_it, so the choices follow c_t = Theta c_t-1 + gamma x_t on the weighted network Theta, without self-links, Eqs. 1.10 and 1.11 of Caiani et al. (2016, Section 1.1.6). The individual characteristic is x_it = x_i + sigma eps_it, with a standard normal shock eps_it. The mean choice follows c_t = (1/N) sum_i d_i c_i,t-1 + gamma x_t (Eq. 1.12), where the out-degree d_i of agent i, the sum of column i of Theta, measures how much its choice moves the others, so the persistence of the aggregate depends on the out-degrees and on how they correlate with the choices. Without shocks the choices settle at (I - Theta)^-1 gamma x when the spectral radius of Theta is below 1.

    The system has the group agents of the choices agents.c and the herding herding. The observable of the system is the mean choice mean_choice.

    def act(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Set the reserve ratio of the banks from the schedule.

    Args:
        system:
            The system view of the regulator.
    """
    before = system.time < system.get_parameter('change_at')
    ratio = system.get_parameter('ratio') if before else system.get_parameter('new_ratio')
    name = f'{self.banks}.reserve_ratio'
    if system.parameters[name] != ratio:
        system.set_parameter(name, ratio)

    PurchasingPowerElement(label, visual=None, *, variables=None, A=A_MATRIX, B=B_MATRIX, C=C_MATRIX, D=D_MATRIX, feedback=False)

    Bases: DeclaredElement

    National economy of three spending sectors, with sector policies.

    It follows z' = A z + B u and y = C z + D u. The state z_i is the gap between the demand and the supply of money of sector i, the basic, the desired, and the luxurious living conditions, the output y_i is the index of the sector, and the policy x_i of a sector is a step of size policy_i at the time policy_time_i. Without feedback the economy takes the policies as its inputs, u = x. With feedback, the market reactions of Forrest's feedback component set u so that every sector responds to its own policy only, as the decoupled systems w_i' = A w_i + B_i x_i and y_i = C_i w_i + D_i x_i, whose states w_ik the element holds. The feedback component holds a copy of z that equals z from the common zero start, so u = D^-1 (y - C z) with the decoupled outputs y.

    def get_inputs(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[Expression]:
    """Return the inputs `u` of the economy.

    They are the policies, or `D^-1 (y - C z)` with feedback.

    Args:
        s:
            The namespace of the economy.

    Returns:
        inputs:
            One input per sector.
    """
    if not self.feedback:
        return self._get_policies(s)
    C, inverse = np.asarray(self.C), np.linalg.inv(np.asarray(self.D, dtype=float))
    z, y = [getattr(s, f'z{i}') for i in range(1, SECTORS + 1)], self.get_outputs(s)
    gaps = [y[i] - sum(C[i, k] * z[k] for k in range(SECTORS)) for i in range(SECTORS)]
    return [sum(inverse[i, k] * gaps[k] for k in range(SECTORS)) for i in range(SECTORS)]

    def get_outputs(self, s: SimpleNamespace) -> list[Expression]:
    """Return the indices `y` of the sectors.

    Args:
        s:
            The namespace of the economy.

    Returns:
        outputs:
            One index per sector.
    """
    x, C, D = self._get_policies(s), np.asarray(self.C), np.asarray(self.D)
    if not self.feedback:
        z = [getattr(s, f'z{i}') for i in range(1, SECTORS + 1)]
        return [sum(C[i, k] * z[k] + D[i, k] * x[k] for k in range(SECTORS)) for i in range(SECTORS)]
    return [
        sum(C[i, k] * getattr(s, f'w{i + 1}{k + 1}') for k in range(SECTORS)) + D[i, i] * x[i]
        for i in range(SECTORS)
    ]

    def lend(self, agent: ReserveBankView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Lend the excess reserves to a random customer.

    The payment is redeposited at a random customer's bank.

    Args:
        agent:
            The bank.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    excess = agent.reserves - system.get_parameter('reserve_ratio') * agent.deposits
    customers = system.get_agents(self.customers, DepositorView)
    own = [customer for customer in customers if customer.get_referenced('bank') is agent]
    if excess <= TOLERANCE or not own:
        return
    borrower = own[int(system.rng.integers(len(own)))]
    payee = customers[int(system.rng.integers(len(customers)))]
    bank = payee.get_referenced('bank')
    if not isinstance(bank, ReserveBankView):
        return
    borrower.loan += excess
    agent.loans += excess
    agent.reserves -= excess
    payee.deposit += excess
    bank.deposits += excess
    bank.reserves += excess

    SettlerElement(label, visual=None, *, food=10.0, money=0.0, loans=0.0, age=20.0, parent=-1.0, employer=-1.0, harvested=0.0, born=-100.0, fate=ALIVE, fertility=0.5, exploration=0.5, enterprise=0.5, restlessness=0.1, labour=5.0, need=2.0, maturity=15.0, lifespan=85.0, spacing=2.0, endowment=5.0, mutation=0.05, sight=5.0, reserve=5.0, monetary=0.0)

    Bases: Element

    Mortal person who eats, ages, raises children, and moves.

    In the monetary economy, the person also works and founds firms. Every step a person eats need food and starves when its food runs out, and past lifespan it dies of old age with probability 1/7. A child takes need food from its parent and follows it. A fed adult has a child with the probability fertility, at most once every spacing steps, and gives it endowment food. The child inherits the four propensities, each moved by a normal mutation and kept in [0, 1]. A person that harvested too little and holds less than reserve steps of food moves, far with the probability exploration. In the monetary economy an unemployed adult on a patch with food but no firm founds one with the probability enterprise, and a worker quits with the probability restlessness.

    def live(self, agent: SettlerView, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Age, eat, die, have children, and move or work.

    Args:
        agent:
            The person.

        system:
            The system.
    """
    agent.age += 1
    adult = agent.age >= agent.maturity
    if not adult:
        self._feed_child(agent, system)
    agent.food -= agent.need
    if agent.food < 0:
        agent.fate = STARVED
        return
    if agent.age > agent.lifespan and system.rng.random() < OLD_AGE_DEATH:
        agent.fate = AGED
        return
    if not adult:
        return
    self._breed(agent, system)
    employed = agent.monetary > 0 and self._work_or_found(agent, system)
    if not employed and agent.harvested < agent.need and agent.food < agent.reserve * agent.need:
        SettlerElement._wander(agent, system, agent.sight)
    agent.harvested = 0.0

    StochasticGrowthElement(label, visual=None, *, K=0.2, regime=0, alpha=1 / 3, beta=0.95, z_low=0.9, z_high=1.1)

    Bases: Element

    Representative economy with capital and a productivity regime.

    Its technology is the Cobb-Douglas Y = z K^alpha. The productivity z is z_low in regime 0 and z_high in regime 1, and a Markov chain of the system moves the regime. With logarithmic utility and full depreciation, the optimal consumption is C = (1 - alpha beta) Y and the capital of the next period is the output saved, K' = alpha beta z K^alpha.

    @staticmethod
def get_consumption(s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
    """Return the optimal consumption `(1 - alpha beta) Y`.

    Args:
        s:
            The namespace of the economy.

    Returns:
        consumption:
            The consumption.
    """
    return (1 - s.alpha * s.beta) * StochasticGrowthElement.get_output(s)

def get_output(s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
    """Return the output `z K^alpha`.

    Args:

            The namespace of the economy.

    @staticmethod
def get_productivity(s: SimpleNamespace) -> Expression:
    """Return the productivity of the current regime.

    Args:
        s:
            The namespace of the economy.

    Returns:
        z:
            The productivity.
    """
    return s.z_low + (s.z_high - s.z_low) * s.regime

    StockFlowConsistentEconomySystem(*, household_deposits=60.0, firm_deposits=20.0, bank_deposits=10.0, loans=50.0, sales=40.0, alpha_income=0.6, alpha_wealth=0.4, wage_share=0.7, interest=0.03, payout=0.5, distribution=0.3, credit=0.1, repayment=0.08, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    A stock-flow consistent economy.

    It is a closed circuit of money between households, firms, and a bank. Money is the deposits of the three sectors, tagged as the quantity money, and every transaction of a period is a flow, so each payment is one sector's outflow and another's inflow. Households consume a share alpha_income of their wages and a share alpha_wealth of their deposits, firms pay the wage share of last period's sales and the interest on their loans, and distribute a share of their deposits as profits, and the bank pays out a share of its funds as dividends. Lending creates money and repayment destroys it, the only flows with the environment, so the total money changes exactly by lending minus repayment, in the spirit of the systems of Godley and Lavoie (2007) and the balance sheets of Caiani et al. (2016). Loans approach credit * sales / repayment and sales settle where the stocks stop growing. The circuit moves the money of a period, and the maps loans and sales set the loans and the sales of the firms.

    The system has the deposits households.deposits, firms.deposits, and bank.deposits, the loans firms.loans, the sales firms.sales, the flows circuit.consumption, circuit.wages, circuit.interest, circuit.dividends, circuit.profits, circuit.lending, and circuit.repayments, the maps loans and sales, and the net money created __boundary.money.

    		 10.0

    The initial loans of the firms.

    		 50.0
    sales float

    The sales of the previous period.

    		 40.0
    alpha_income float

    The propensity to consume out of wages.

    		 0.6
    alpha_wealth float

    The propensity to consume out of deposits.

    		 0.4
    wage_share float

    The share of sales paid as wages.

    The interest rate on loans per period.

    		 0.03
    payout float

    		 0.3

    ToyFirmInvestmentSystem(n_firms=100, *, gamma=1.1, phi=0.1, r=0.1, pbar=0.01, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Heterogeneous firms that invest out of past profits and sell at random prices.

    Firms enter and exit. The firms start with net worth and capital 1 and a profit drawn from pbar + 2 U(0, 1), as in the toy system of Bargigli et al. in Caiani et al. (2016, sect. 2.1). Aggregate production fluctuates as bankrupt firms are replaced. The system has the group firms and the aggregate production production.
